topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the core themes of the lecture including evolutionary selection, cellular origin, and microenvironmental influences alongside the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cell-intrinsic genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cell-intrinsic alterations confer selective fitness advantages and activate tumorigenic programs to drive clonal expansion.

topics.label: Cell of origin and stem cell hierarchies in tumor initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of tissue hierarchy and stemness properties in determining which cell types initiate and propagate tumors.

topics.label: Inflammatory microenvironmental promotion of incipient tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how external and local inflammatory signals act as promoters to induce stem-like oncogenic programs in cells carrying pre-existing mutations.

topics.label: Stromal dependency in established tumors and therapeutic targeting
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how established neoplasms depend on non-malignant microenvironmental cells for growth and how these interactions offer targets for therapy.

topics.label: Methodologies for investigating tumor evolution and spatial architecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews the genomic, spatial transcriptomic, and computational techniques used to map cellular interactions and evolutionary lineages in tumors.

topics.label: Integrated multi-factorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesises how genetic mutations, cellular origins, transcriptional plasticity, and microenvironmental forces converge to drive malignant progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer delivers concluding remarks and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
